text: In June 2020, we converged. 38 of us named "the justice act," first offered by Tim Scott; 38 of us also named "justice in policing act," the measure we rose to answer. We assembled our name from a line — "unifying solutions to invigorate communities everywhere" — carried by 24 of us from the seventeenth on, first put forward by Mitch McConnell. 28 of us returned, as we had since before this era, to "law enforcement officers." 24 of us spoke "of george floyd," a phrase already in the record before we reached it. By the twenty-fifth we peaked. Two measures moved through these weeks — ours, and "floyd justice in policing act" — in the vocabulary of policing. We spoke, in the end, the words the moment handed us.
